clue.text: Incontinent cows showing lack of power of voluntary motion

definitions.text: lack of power of voluntary motion

indicators.note: split after its first syllable, this word reads as the preposition in followed by a noun, so the cattle are placed inside

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent
kine is an archaic plural of cow

explanation.surface: Cattle that cannot control their bowels are oddly described as lacking voluntary movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incontinent' must be split as 'In continent': the cows sit inside a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Akinesia is the medical term for loss or impairment of the ability to move muscles at will.

clue.text: Failing to support a director's recommendation

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath the others

parts.note: taken as written
D is a standard abbreviation for director
a vice is a failing or moral weakness

explanation.surface: A director's suggestion fails to win backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a verb but is a noun here, a fault of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance offered to someone about what they should do, the same thing as a recommendation.

clue.text: Serial broadcast in the country

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into new positions

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A radio or television serial is being transmitted nationwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a Middle Eastern nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Bloke with bird on the street

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece being on another means it sits above it

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite
St is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A man walks down the road carrying a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloke' defines a man's given name, here Ernest, as a typical male name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it stands for a typical chap or fellow.

clue.text: Fashionable team went forward

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a side is a team in sport
left is a past tense meaning departed or went

explanation.surface: A stylish squad advanced up the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like part of 'went forward', but it is the definition: an inside left was an attacking football position.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside left was a forward position in old football formations, playing between centre forward and outside left.

clue.text: Flier to obstruct venture

parts.note: to bar is to block or obstruct
to venture money is to bet it

explanation.surface: A pilot sets out to block a risky undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot or a leaflet; here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbet is a tropical bird, and birds are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Is skilled at getting round girl; that's charming

indicators.note: getting round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to be able is to have the skill
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man adept at winning a girl over is called charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable describes someone delightful and appealing, which is what charming means.

clue.text: Weave corsets producing tension on ship

parts.note: to bob and to weave are paired dodging moves in boxing
stays are an old name for a corset

explanation.surface: Knitting undergarments creates stress aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weave' seems to be about cloth, but it is the boxer's sideways dodge, as in 'bob and weave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobstays are ropes or chains holding a ship's bowsprit down, so they apply tension on a vessel.

clue.text: Initially teachers half-heartedly comfort trusted servant

indicators.note: with half the heart missing, one of the two central letters is dropped
initially points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of teachers
to reassure is to comfort

explanation.surface: Teachers half-heartedly console a loyal assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: REASSURE has SS at its heart; removing half of it leaves REASURE, giving TREASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a valued helper or domestic servant a treasure is an idiom for someone indispensable and reliable.

clue.text: Person in poem is a painter

indicators.note: in places one element inside another

parts.note: a verse is a poem
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A character in a poem turns out to be an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a Venetian Renaissance artist known for large canvases such as The Wedding at Cana.

clue.text: Patch together a fishing boat touring Belgium

indicators.note: touring a place means travelling around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a coble is a flat-bottomed fishing boat of north-east England
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: Someone improvises repairs to a boat as it sails round Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: To cobble something together is an idiom for making it roughly or hastily from whatever is available.

clue.text: Unfaithful lover in novel is scared

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cheating partner in a book is frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but here it means new, signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida, in Chaucer and Shakespeare, betrays her lover Troilus for Diomedes, making her the type of inconstancy.

clue.text: Finished one small drink

parts.note: past means over or finished
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone has drained a single little drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French aperitif, usually served with water.

clue.text: The drama teacher's carriage?

parts.note: surface reading: the way an acting tutor holds themselves, or the vehicle they own
setter's reading: a coach for the theatre, which split differently names an old horse-drawn passenger vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a coach who trains people for the stage, and a coach that ran between towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach was a horse-drawn public carriage running scheduled routes between staging posts.

clue.text: Sportsman embraced old workman

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a player is someone who takes part in a sport
late means former or old, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: An athlete hugged an elderly labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A platelayer is a railway worker who lays and maintains track, a kind of manual labourer.

clue.text: New sergeant is set at odds

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A recently arrived NCO has fallen out with the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them hostile or distant from each other, causing a falling-out.

clue.text: The sailor's to go astray when on the drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece being on another places it on top

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard sailor
to sin is to stray from the right path
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman tends to misbehave when drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the drink' reads like being on a binge, but in a down entry 'on' places the sailor and his straying above the opening word of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, famous in nineteenth-century Paris.

clue.text: 22 surrounds church fence

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: the answer to 22 across
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced bandit encloses a church boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' looks like a boundary but is slang for a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver of stolen goods buys loot from thieves, exactly the criminal role a fence plays.

clue.text: Deception begs future involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests things entangled together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A trick invites later entanglement.
explanation.definitionFit: Subterfuge is trickery or evasion used to achieve an aim, which is a form of deceit.

clue.text: Footwear worn by Oriental stars

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone wraps around them, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: boots are footwear
E for east, so oriental

explanation.surface: Shoes on the feet of an Eastern celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Boötes, the Herdsman, is a northern constellation containing the bright star Arcturus, a group of stars.

clue.text: Wizard often having a stoop

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small falcon, which dives on prey in a stoop

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a hunched old wizard; a stoop is also a falcon's steep dive onto prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is Arthur's magician in legend, and also the name of a small falcon that hunts by swooping.

clue.text: Against separating unreactive type of sugar

indicators.note: something separating a word sits between its letters, splitting it apart

parts.note: inert means chemically unreactive
V for versus, against

explanation.surface: A chemist opposes splitting a sluggish kind of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Invert sugar is a syrup of glucose and fructose made by splitting sucrose, used in baking and confectionery.

clue.text: Banker transfixed by English brigand

indicators.note: something transfixed is pierced through, so another piece is driven inside it

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A financier is pinned down by an English bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests a financier but means a river, since a river has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reivers were raiders on the Anglo-Scottish border who stole cattle, so they were outlaws and bandits.

clue.text: Caroline's nasty chemical

indicators.note: nasty implies something spoiled or twisted, so the letters are wrenched out of order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A woman named Caroline has an unpleasant substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrolein is a toxic, pungent compound formed when fats are overheated, an organic aldehyde.

clue.text: Time to interrupt credulous resident

indicators.note: interrupting something breaks into its middle, so one piece is placed inside

parts.note: naive means credulous or easily taken in
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is time to cut short a gullible local.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a place and living there, so an inhabitant or local person.

clue.text: Work the land in infamous prison

indicators.note: in places one element inside another

parts.note: base means low and dishonourable, so infamous
to till is to plough and cultivate soil

explanation.surface: Convicts farm the soil inside a notorious jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infamous prison' reads as one phrase, but 'infamous' is wordplay and the definition is just 'prison'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state jail, stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Old journalist and artist in seated room

parts.note: ex means former, so old
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A retired reporter and a painter sit together in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An exedra is a recess or room with seats around its wall, used in classical buildings for conversation.

clue.text: Enthusiast is after trunk of tree

indicators.note: coming after another piece places this one second in the line

parts.note: a trunk is a large storage chest
a nut is a fan or enthusiast

explanation.surface: A tree lover is pursuing the trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' seems to belong to the tree, but it is a box for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: The chestnut is a broadleaf tree bearing edible or horse nuts, so it is a species of tree.
